_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); gas distribution and midstream signals with ONEOK's rule-T thresholds

pit_profile.why: 'We are a leading midstream service provider and own one of the nation’s premier NGL systems, connecting NGL supply in the Rocky Mountain, Permian and Mid-Continent regions with key market centers and an extensive network of natural gas gathering, processing, storage and transportation assets.' 'We operate primarily fee-based businesses in each of our three reportable segments, and our consolidated earnings were approximately 90% fee-based in 2019.' 'The volatility of natural gas, crude oil and NGL prices could affect adversely our earnings and cash flows.' (the FY2019 10-K's own words; it does not use the word cyclical, so DURABLE, the MU rule); no disruption theme in the registry is live for a midstream company on this date (of the live themes, OFFSHORE is scoped to 'lower-cost offshore delivery (Indian IT services) takes share and price from Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing', CLOUD to 'public cloud displaces on-premise hardware, storage, legacy databases and data-center outsourcing', ECOMMERCE to 'e-commerce (Amazon effect) displaces physical retail, malls, grocery, distribution', STREAMING to 'cord-cutting / streaming displaces linear TV networks and pay-TV bundles', ENERGY_TRANSITION to 'decarbonisation strands oil, gas and coal reserves and refining', EV to 'battery-electric vehicles displace ICE powertrains, auto parts suppliers and fuel retail', CRYPTO to 'crypto / DeFi disintermediates payments networks, banks, exchanges, remittance': none names gas distribution or midstream), so the watch list is empty; ENERGY_TRANSITION's reserves and refining are out of scope (the TRGP and BKR reading): ONEOK holds no reserves of its own and refines nothing ('We may not be able to accurately estimate hydrocarbon reserves and production volumes expected to be delivered to us for a variety of reasons, including the unavailability of sufficiently detailed information and unanticipated changes in producers’ expected drilling schedules.'); its greenhouse gas risk factor: 'We may face significant costs to comply with the regulation of GHG emissions.' (text only); its climate-demand risk factor: 'Changes in regulatory policies, public sentiment or technology due to the threat of climate change that result in a reduction in the demand for hydrocarbon products, restrictions on their use, or increased use of renewable energy could reduce future demand for hydrocarbons and reduce volumes available to us for gathering, processing, fractionation, transportation, storage and marketing.' (text only: the volumes are its producers'); EV and CRYPTO are out of scope: the 10-K names neither electric vehicles nor crypto (text only)

BEAR.desc: EPS -22.8%/yr (worst year FY10-FY19, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS -10.9%/yr (Q3 revenues + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +18.6%/yr (FY10-FY19 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +54.3%/yr (best 2-yr run FY10-FY19, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: OKE (retrospective, 2021-02-12) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.65x (57.9% downside to Bear $19 / +88.4% upside to Bull $85) | Adj composite 2.36 vs market 2.29: gap +0.07 [FAIRLY VALUED] | +25% above the EPP floor $36 (23x FY20E $1.57) | Conservative 2-yr case: +21.6% total (+10.8%/yr) | At 28.7x FY20E the 15% hurdle price $60 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; net margin +7.1% and Distribution operating income n/r in Q3 2020, forward revenues -3.9% (no FY20 revenue guide in numbers, Q3 2020 revenues as reported); no theme in the registry is live for a midstream company on this date (CLOUD and OFFSHORE are scoped to IT, ECOMMERCE to retail, STREAMING to TV, ENERGY_TRANSITION to reserves and refining, EV to fuel retail, CRYPTO to payments and banks).
